title: Relative ampleness of an invertible sheaf is insensitive to thickening the source and the base
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter more-morphisms.tex (More on Morphisms), section on thickenings and ample sheaves
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-morphisms.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261011
difficulty_reason: The lemma is about a morphism of thickenings (f, f') : (X subset X') -> (S subset S') and an invertible sheaf L' on X' whose restriction to X is L; it asserts that L' is f'-ample if and only if L is f-ample (statement lines 311-318). The proof works by moving to the base: relative ampleness is a condition on affine opens of the base, the thickening gives a bijection between the affine opens of S and of S', and after that reduction the claim becomes the statement that ampleness survives reduction along a thickening, which is the cited Limits lemma (proof lines 320-331). The non-routine step is the first one, because it is the correspondence of affine opens under a thickening that lets an honest relative statement be tested in the affine situation. The proof is short and complete, with the cited Limits lemma as its only external input, so H2.
